_comment: What the Glama listing was last released with, and what the tools are NOW. Glama scores the tool definitions and publishes that score against a release version, so when these change the listing describes tools that no longer exist. cmd/heliograph/glama_snapshot_test.go fails when they drift and says what to do. Creating a Glama release needs a person: the admin route redirects to /sign-up even with a valid API key.

tools.name: heliograph_doctor
tools.description: Check whether the transport works from here, and change nothing. Run this before a long step: read access is not write access, and finding out afterwards costs a whole round trip through somebody who cannot debug the machine.

tools.name: heliograph_estates
tools.description: List the configured estates and the transport each uses. Call this first when you do not know which estate to act on.

tools.name: heliograph_gaps
tools.description: Where a run stalled. Returns the intervals in the log's timestamp column, longest first, each attributed to the line BEFORE it, which is what was running. Do this before reading a long log: a hang and slow progress are indistinguishable without it. If every line carries the same timestamp the capture was buffered and the log cannot answer the question at all, which this reports as an error.

tools.name: heliograph_logs
tools.description: List the captured logs, newest first. Each name carries the request id that produced it, so the log for a run you sent is the one whose name matches the id heliograph_send returned. Use this to find a log; use heliograph_read_log to read one.

tools.name: heliograph_read_log
tools.description: Read a captured log whole. Every line carries a UTC timestamp. Read all of it, including the parts that worked: a passing probe beside a failing one is the control that says what the failure means. A green exit means the probes that ran passed, not that the work happened.

tools.name: heliograph_send
tools.description: Publish a step for the station to run, and return immediately. This does NOT wait for the result: poll heliograph_status with the id this returns until it reports a terminal state, then read the log. The station decides whether to run it at all: a step that declares no mode is refused, and one that changes state needs CONFIRM=yes and a station started with --allow-actions.

tools.name: heliograph_status
tools.description: What the station is doing now. State is one of starting, running, idle, cancelled, refused, stopped or undelivered. Five of those are terminal: idle, cancelled, refused, stopped and undelivered. `starting` and `running` mean the run is still going. An empty state means the station has published nothing yet, which usually means it has not been started. A state you do not recognise is neither finished nor alive: a newer station may publish one, so keep polling rather than giving up. `refused` is not a failure: it means the station would not run the step, and the reason names the flag that would permit it. `undelivered` means the run finished and the log is complete but the transport would not take it, so waiting for more is exactly wrong.

_listingIsBehind: The listing was released at 0.3.2 and describes 0.3.2's heliograph_status. That description was WRONG - it named five states where status.go has seven, and told a caller to poll until one of four terminal states, omitting `undelivered`, which status.go:121 makes terminal and whose comment says waiting is exactly the wrong response. The correction could not wait for a Glama session, so `toolsDigest` and `tools` here are the CURRENT definitions and drift detection still catches the next change. THE OUTSTANDING HUMAN STEP is a Build and Release at https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/heliograph-io/heliograph/admin/dockerfile, after which `releasedVersion` becomes that version and this field goes. heliograph-cloud#267. Since then (heliograph-io/heliograph#147): heliograph_status takes an optional `id` and says `not picked up yet` for a status about any other request, and heliograph_send tells the caller to poll with that id. The same Build and Release covers both. And (heliograph-io/heliograph#149): heliograph_send takes optional `mode` and `expires`, and now writes the same target and 24-hour expiry the CLI does.
